A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the neutrino fluxes from these six microquasar sources are not detectable with the current ANTARES data, and that the current upper limits are already constraining some of the theoretical models.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the ANTARES data do not show any evidence for neutrino emission correlated in time with the microquasar activity, which implies that the neutrino emission is either too weak to be detected by the present generation of neutrino telescopes, or that it is produced in a different mechanism than that proposed in the models.

the ANTARES data are consistent with the absence of time dependent neutrino fluxes from the microquasar jets, and therefore the models predicting a strong neutrino emission from these objects need to be reconsidered.

the neutrino fluence upper limits derived from the ANTARES data are competitive with the ones from other experiments, and that they can be used to put constraints on the proton luminosity in the jet of the microquasar.
